summary: Independently reconstructed the PCAE strategic roadmap from primary sources (Phase 144H's Publication Chapter Retrospective/System Execution Readiness Assessment/Roadmap Re-Baseline, Phase 145I's Interactive Workflow chapter certification, CHGR-001 v1.0, IWPC-001 v1.4, and direct inspection of src/pcae/governance/publication/record.py) rather than assuming Chapter 146's scope. Determined Track 145 (Interactive Workflow) ends where it does because it delivered 144H's own highest-priority, lowest-risk recommendation (a CLI/transport surface for the already-frozen, already-verified governed decision-making stack) in full, certified CERTIFIED WITH OBSERVATIONS with zero open Blocking findings. Defined Chapter 146 as CHGR-001 Sec.9 schema-envelope/canonical-identity conformance for the Publication Coordinator's output: 144G independently found the human_governance_record sub-object is missing 14 of 19 fields human_governance_record.schema.json requires (schema_id, schema_version, contract_version, record_digest, authority_basis_claimed, assurance_level, lifecycle_state, confirmation_evidence_ref, provenance_ref, integrity_ref, limitations, extensions, plus two others), disclosed explicitly in record.py's own docstring/_KNOWN_LIMITATIONS, not a hidden defect. This is 144H's own second-ranked, still-open Future Chapter Recommendation, now that recommendation #1 (Interactive Workflow CLI) is delivered. Scoped the chapter to close the schema-envelope fields with no unresolved design question, while explicitly re-disclosing (not resolving) authority_basis_claimed/assurance_level as a distinct, deferred sub-problem tied to IWPC-001 Sec.31's own standing deferral of the authority-evaluation gap (informally 'C-1') to a future, separately governed initiative -- guarding against this chapter silently absorbing C-1's full scope. Considered and rejected three alternative candidates (re-deriving the Phase 107A execution-capability gap analysis; roadmap-tracking reconciliation between pcae roadmap/docs/ROADMAP.md/PROJECT_STATUS.md; resuming GLP-PILOT-C6) as either not chapter-scale or lower-priority per 144H's own explicit ranking; confirmed Runtime/Permission Broker execution capability itself remains correctly ranked last per docs/ROADMAP.md Principle 10 ('Pluggable first...Executable last') and 144H's own reasoning. Produced full architectural analysis (context, motivation, problem statement, design principles, decomposition, ownership model, interfaces, invariants, extensibility model, security/operational considerations) and a recommended seven-phase governance sequence (146B Contract Freeze through 146H Certification), mirroring the 137G-137N/145A-145I precedent. Architecture only: zero production/contract/runtime files modified; no execution capability added; runtime confirmed unchanged (Observed/observe/unavailable) at both phase start and close. See docs/PHASE_146A_NEXT_PCAE_CHAPTER_ARCHITECTURE.md.
